answer: The nectar multiplier is published, charged in ridge, and sonnet lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 15 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3092 identities would post 2592 proofs and burn roughly 85 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
